evi.interpretation: Corrects for atmospheric haze and canopy background — more reliable than NDVI in high-biomass (dense canopy) areas where NDVI saturates.
evi.label: EVI — Enhanced Vegetation Index

mndwi.interpretation: Higher = more water. Better than NDWI at suppressing built-up/soil noise, standard choice for urban or mixed-landuse water mapping.
mndwi.label: MNDWI — Modified NDWI

msavi2.formula: (2xNIR + 1 - sqrt((2xNIR + 1)^2 - 8x(NIR - Red))) / 2  with NIR = B8, Red = B4
msavi2.interpretation: A soil-adjusted vegetation index whose soil factor adjusts itself (SAVI uses a fixed L): suited to sparse vegetation and fields dominated by bare soil, where NDVI is biased by soil brightness. It reduces soil noise at the cost of a smaller dynamic range than NDVI.
msavi2.label: MSAVI2 — Modified Soil-Adjusted Vegetation Index

nbr.interpretation: High for healthy vegetation, low or negative for burnt or very dry ground (SWIR2 rises and NIR falls after burning). This is a single-date value: burn severity needs the difference between a pre-fire and a post-fire date (dNBR), which the Burn Severity tool computes.
nbr.label: NBR — Normalized Burn Ratio

ndbi.interpretation: Higher = more built-up/impervious surface. Bare soil can also read positive — cross-check against NDVI to separate the two.
ndbi.label: NDBI — Normalized Difference Built-up Index

ndmi.citation: Gao 1996 (published as NDWI; also called NDMI)
ndmi.interpretation: Follows the water content of vegetation canopies: higher = wetter canopy, lower = drier or water-stressed vegetation. NOT the open-water NDWI above (McFeeters, Green/NIR): do not use it to map water bodies. It is the NDWI used inside the NDDI drought index. Compare a place with its own earlier values; no single threshold separates stressed from healthy across crops.
ndmi.label: NDMI — Normalized Difference Moisture Index (Gao's NDWI)

ndre.interpretation: A red-edge index that follows leaf chlorophyll content, so it keeps responding in dense, mature canopies where NDVI saturates. It tracks chlorophyll (greenness), not nitrogen directly: a low value can come from nitrogen shortage but equally from water stress, disease or growth stage. B5 is a 20 m band, resampled to 10 m.
ndre.label: NDRE — Normalized Difference Red Edge Index

ndsi.interpretation: Same band math as MNDWI, different interpretation context: NDSI > 0.4 is the standard threshold for classifying a pixel as snow/ice-covered.
ndsi.label: NDSI — Normalized Difference Snow Index

ndvi.interpretation: Higher = denser/healthier green vegetation. <0 typically water/cloud/snow, 0-0.2 bare soil/sparse veg, 0.2-0.5 moderate, >0.5 dense vegetation.
ndvi.label: NDVI — Normalized Difference Vegetation Index

ndwi.interpretation: Higher = more open water. Tuned for open water bodies; can under-detect water in built-up areas — use MNDWI there instead.
ndwi.label: NDWI — Normalized Difference Water Index (McFeeters)

savi.formula: ((NIR - Red) / (NIR + Red + L)) x (1 + L), L = 0.5
savi.interpretation: NDVI corrected for soil brightness — preferred over NDVI in sparse-vegetation/arid AOIs where bare soil otherwise skews the index.
savi.label: SAVI — Soil-Adjusted Vegetation Index
